commits.message:
fix(live): full-height inline frame no longer leaks rows into scrollback (rich-live-4rh) (#248)

* fix(live): paint inline frames through App's painter, cursor on the last row (rich-live-4rh)

An inline Live wrote a newline after its frame's last row. On a frame as
tall as the terminal that newline scrolled the screen, and the next erase
could not reach the frame's first row, so every refresh left it in
scrollback. App already painted correctly with the cursor resting on the
last row. The painter now lives in core/paint.ts and both paint through it
(rich-live-4vwq); the newline under the frame is written once, on hand-back.

Live's tests now drive @xterm/headless (new devDependency) and assert the
screen and scrollback a user would see.

* fix(paint): one Painter owns the rewind count, the width crop and the hand-back (rich-live-4rh)

A restarted inline Live painted over the frame it had handed back, because
Live never reset the row count App resets on resume. Painter now holds that
count from take() to handBack(), crops rows to the screen for both callers,
and owns the surface's enter/leave bytes. Each row starts with its own CR, so
a Live handed back before any frame no longer moves the cursor.

Review: /code-review high on #248.
